# mod_pagespeed

> Self-hosted web performance optimization for Apache and nginx. Open source under the Apache License 2.0. mod_pagespeed 2 converges the mod_pagespeed lineage and the engine from the 2.0 re-architecture into one product: a native web-server module with a separate optimizer worker.

We-Amp B.V. develops mod_pagespeed 2, the converged continuation of the open-source mod_pagespeed project, originally developed at Google. It automatically optimizes web content (images, CSS, JavaScript, HTML): a native in-process module for Apache and nginx handles serving, and a separate optimizer worker does the heavy optimization work outside the web server. Drop-in compatible with the classic module: the same configuration directives and filters carry over, and no application code changes are required. mod_pagespeed 2 converges the 1.15 module line (renumbered from 1.1, the forward-semver successor to the last upstream release, 1.14.36.1) with the ModPageSpeed 2.0 engine, which continues as the optimizer worker; both predecessor lines upgrade to it in place.

Heritage: mod_pagespeed, the open-source optimization core this product continues, powers 231,341 live sites (per BuiltWith, May 2026; 1.9 million+ across its history). These are not We-Amp customers; they are the proof the optimization core works at scale.

What it does:

- Image optimization in the optimizer worker: WebP, AVIF and SVG transcoding, viewport-aware resizing, learned per-format quality prediction with SSIMULACRA2 verification, content-aware classification and denoising, up to 37 variants per image (36 raster plus one SVG)
- CSS optimization: minification, heuristic critical-CSS extraction with an optional headless-browser pipeline, non-blocking stylesheet loading
- JavaScript optimization: safe minification and browser-analysis-driven script deferral, no AST transforms
- HTML optimization: critical CSS injection, 103 Early Hints, lazy-loading attributes, image dimensions, LCP image preload, font preloading, preconnect hints
- Variant-aware caching keyed on a 32-bit capability mask (image format, viewport, pixel density, Save-Data, transfer encoding), served zero-copy from the shared Cyclone cache
- The module's classic filter set: CSS and JavaScript combining, image spriting, in-place resource optimization, domain mapping, and the built-in admin console

mod_pagespeed is open source under the Apache License 2.0: free to install and run, in development and in production, with free standard signed packages. What We-Amp sells is support, in three tiers; Priority and Enterprise add a private package repository (being set up):

- Standard support — a direct channel to the engineers who build the product, for up to 5 production servers; €490 a year; First response within 2 business days
- Priority support — everything in Standard plus a private package repository (being set up), for up to 25 production servers; €1,900 a year; First response next business day; severity 1 (production down) within 8 business hours
- Enterprise — everything in Priority plus a named engineer, custom build targets and backports, for unlimited servers and sites in one organization; from €7,500 a year; Severity 1 (production down) within 4 business hours; other severities per agreement
- Prices are per year, billed annually, excl. VAT. The price you sign at holds for one year. Existing customers keep their current rate; nobody is repriced mid-term. Response targets are first-response times. Support runs on CET business days, and business hours are CET.
- Standard and Priority are bought at checkout; Enterprise runs on a master agreement. A fixed-price agent-readiness audit is also available: one site, one written report, one review call, €950 per site excl. VAT.
- No bandwidth fees, no per-request charges, no feature gates; the software itself costs nothing. Support terms: https://we-amp.com/licensing/

Every documentation page and every filter reference page below is also served as Markdown at its URL with a `.md` suffix (for example https://modpagespeed.com/docs/getting-started.md and https://modpagespeed.com/docs/filters/rewrite_images.md; the filters table is https://modpagespeed.com/docs/filters.md), and https://modpagespeed.com/llms-full.txt carries this index followed by the full text of every one of those pages. Every blog post is served as Markdown the same way (https://modpagespeed.com/blog/<slug>.md) and is listed in the Blog section below, but its text is not in llms-full.txt: the posts are dated commentary, so fetch one when you need it.

We-Amp B.V., The Netherlands (founded 2012, KvK 57898138); info@we-amp.com for support, partnerships and consulting; security@modpagespeed.com for vulnerability reports only. License: Apache License 2.0; the LICENSE, NOTICE and THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES files ship with every distribution. mod_pagespeed is an open-source project originally developed at Google. mod_pagespeed is developed by We-Amp B.V. and is not affiliated with or endorsed by Google.

## Start here

- [Getting started](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/getting-started/): Pick an integration and get mod_pagespeed serving optimized pages: Apache or nginx module, Docker, IIS or ASP.NET Core, then run the same check.
- [Is it working?](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/is-it-working/): Confirm mod_pagespeed is active: the response header per server, MISS then HIT, ?PageSpeed=off, the admin console and the worker health endpoint.

## Install

- [Install the module on Apache and nginx](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/installation-module/): Install the native mod_pagespeed module for Apache and nginx from the signed package repository: distributions, nginx compatibility, worker pairing.
- [Install with Docker](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/installation-docker/): Run mod_pagespeed with Docker Compose: the nginx module, the worker and a shared Cyclone cache. A one-container quick try, then a production stack.
- [Deploy with Helm](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/helm-deployment/): Install mod_pagespeed on Kubernetes with the official Helm chart: a two-container pod (module + optimizer worker), values, autoscaling and upgrades.
- [cPanel / EasyApache 4](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/cpanel/): Install, uninstall and maintain mod_pagespeed on cPanel / EasyApache 4: the signed EA4 RPM, WHM setup, the cpanel/elevate runbook and ea-apache24 updates.
- [Install on IIS](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/install-iis/): Install the mod_pagespeed IIS module on Windows Server: requirements, the signed MSI, IIS Express, the optional optimizer service and the first check.
- [Envoy HTTP filter (experimental)](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/install-envoy/): PageSpeed for Envoy is an experimental HTTP filter built from the public source repository, not a packaged release: configuration, checks, known limits.
- [Install ASP.NET Core middleware](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/aspnet-getting-started/): Install the mod_pagespeed ASP.NET Core middleware via NuGet — the same optimization pipeline (image transcoding, critical CSS) inside your .NET app.
- [Install with a coding agent](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/agent-install/): Machine-readable install recipes for coding agents, one per server: prerequisites, install, configure, verify and roll back, plus an install skill.

## Upgrade and migrate

- [Upgrade and migrate](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/upgrade/): Upgrade mod_pagespeed per shape: apt or dnf, Docker tag, Helm, the Windows installer and NuGet; what to read first, security updates, rollback.
- [Migrate from ModPageSpeed 2.0](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/migrating-to-2-1/): Move a ModPageSpeed 2.0 Docker Compose or Helm deployment to mod_pagespeed: unprivileged worker, loopback-bound API, configuration carries over.
- [Migrate from mod_pagespeed 1.15](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/migrate-from-1-15/): Move a 1.15 install to mod_pagespeed 2 in place: one package upgrade brings the optimizer worker, configuration carries over, the old cache stays.
- [Migrate from ngx_pagespeed](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/migrate-from-ngx-pagespeed/): Replace an open-source ngx_pagespeed build, compiled in or from a third-party package, with the signed mod_pagespeed 2 nginx module: what carries over.
- [Migrate from IISpeed](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/migrate-from-iispeed/): Move an IISpeed install to the mod_pagespeed IIS module: save the configuration, uninstall IISpeed, run the MSI, keep the cache, verify, roll back.
- [Migrate from the archived Google module](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/migrate-from-google-mod-pagespeed/): Move from the archived mod_pagespeed or ngx_pagespeed binaries to mod_pagespeed 2: package swap, what maps to what, cache, rollback.
- [Long-standing upstream issues resolved](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/upstream-issues-resolved/): Open issues in the archived mod_pagespeed and ngx_pagespeed trackers that current mod_pagespeed resolves, with each fix and the release that shipped it.

## Configure

- [Configuration reference: Apache and nginx directives](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/configuration/): Every mod_pagespeed directive for the native Apache and nginx module, generated from the source: syntax, default, context and description.
- [Set Cache-Control headers](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/cache-control/): Which Cache-Control headers to set on your origin, by content type and by framework, for correct caching with mod_pagespeed.
- [Worker and reverse-proxy configuration](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/worker-configuration/): Every optimizer worker flag and thin nginx module directive of mod_pagespeed (the Docker and reverse-proxy shape), generated from the source.
- [Choose a cache mode: safe vs aggressive](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/cache-modes/): Safe or aggressive Cache-Control for optimized responses in mod_pagespeed, plus the module cache reference: Cyclone, memcached, Redis, purging, IPRO.
- [Integrate with a CDN](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/cdn-integration/): Run mod_pagespeed behind Cloudflare, CloudFront or Fastly: how Vary headers affect edge caching, per-CDN cache-key settings and keeping hit rates high.
- [Domain configuration](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/domain-configuration/): Domain mapping in mod_pagespeed on nginx, Apache and IIS: Domain, MapOriginDomain, MapRewriteDomain, MapProxyDomain, ShardDomain and LoadFromFile.
- [HTTPS configuration](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/https-configuration/): Fetch HTTPS resources on nginx, Apache and IIS with mod_pagespeed: FetchHttps with certificate checks, MapOriginDomain to HTTP, or LoadFromFile.
- [IIS configuration](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/iis-configuration/): mod_pagespeed on IIS via pagespeed.config, the native IIS module and successor to IISpeed: directive syntax, path matching, server and site-level config.
- [ASP.NET Core settings](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/aspnet-configuration/): Configuration reference for the mod_pagespeed ASP.NET Core middleware: appsettings.json PageSpeed options, cache and worker settings, and hot reload.

## Filters

- [Filter selection](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/filter-selection/): Choose which mod_pagespeed filters run: RewriteLevel presets, the CoreFilters default, EnableFilters, DisableFilters, ForbidFilters and thresholds.
- [Image filters](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/image-filters/): Image filters in mod_pagespeed for Apache, nginx and IIS: recompression, WebP and opt-in AVIF conversion, resizing, lazy loading and responsive images.
- [CSS filters](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/css-filters/): CSS filters in mod_pagespeed: minify, combine, inline and flatten @import CSS, plus critical-CSS extraction. Apache, nginx and IIS syntax with tuning.
- [JavaScript filters](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/javascript-filters/): Minify, combine, inline, and defer JavaScript in mod_pagespeed. Directives, defaults, and the trade-offs for each JS filter on Apache, nginx, and IIS.
- [HTML filters](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/html-filters/): HTML optimization filters in mod_pagespeed: collapse whitespace, strip comments, elide attributes, DNS prefetch, and resource preload hints.
- [Rule packs](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/rule-packs/): Rule packs for Apache, nginx and IIS: JSON rules for the canonical, title, description, hreflang and JSON-LD of your pages, in report mode first.
- [Collapse whitespace (collapse_whitespace)](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/filters/collapse_whitespace/): Removes excess whitespace from HTML.
- [Combine CSS (combine_css)](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/filters/combine_css/): Combines multiple CSS files into one.
- [Combine heads (combine_heads)](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/filters/combine_heads/): Merges multiple <head> elements.
- [Combine JavaScript (combine_javascript)](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/filters/combine_javascript/): Combines multiple JS files into one.
- [Convert GIF to PNG (convert_gif_to_png)](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/filters/convert_gif_to_png/): Converts GIF to PNG.
- [Convert JPEG to WebP (convert_jpeg_to_webp)](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/filters/convert_jpeg_to_webp/): Converts JPEG to WebP for capable browsers.
- [Convert PNG to JPEG (convert_png_to_jpeg)](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/filters/convert_png_to_jpeg/): Converts PNG to JPEG when no transparency.
- [Deduplicate inlined images (dedup_inlined_images)](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/filters/dedup_inlined_images/): Replaces repeated inlined images with JS reference.
- [Defer JavaScript (defer_javascript)](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/filters/defer_javascript/): Defers JS execution until after page load.
- [In-place browser optimization (in_place_optimize_for_browser)](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/filters/in_place_optimize_for_browser/): Browser-specific in-place optimization.
- [Inline CSS (inline_css)](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/filters/inline_css/): Inlines small external CSS into HTML.
- [Inline images (inline_images)](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/filters/inline_images/): Inlines small images as data: URIs.
- [Inline JavaScript (inline_javascript)](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/filters/inline_javascript/): Inlines small external JS into HTML.
- [Inline preview images (inline_preview_images)](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/filters/inline_preview_images/): Inserts low-quality image placeholders.
- [Insert DNS prefetch (insert_dns_prefetch)](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/filters/insert_dns_prefetch/): Adds <link rel=dns-prefetch> for third-party domains.
- [Insert image dimensions (insert_image_dimensions)](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/filters/insert_image_dimensions/): Adds width and height attributes to <img> tags.
- [Insert speculation rules (insert_speculation_rules)](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/filters/insert_speculation_rules/): Injects a same-origin prefetch speculation-rules script.
- [Lazy-load images (lazyload_images)](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/filters/lazyload_images/): Defers offscreen image loading.
- [Local storage cache (local_storage_cache)](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/filters/local_storage_cache/): Caches inlined resources in localStorage.
- [Move CSS above scripts (move_css_above_scripts)](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/filters/move_css_above_scripts/): Moves CSS <link> above <script> tags.
- [Move CSS to head (move_css_to_head)](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/filters/move_css_to_head/): Moves CSS <link> into <head>.
- [Outline CSS (outline_css)](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/filters/outline_css/): Externalizes large inline CSS blocks.
- [Outline JavaScript (outline_javascript)](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/filters/outline_javascript/): Externalizes large inline JS blocks.
- [Prioritize critical CSS (prioritize_critical_css)](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/filters/prioritize_critical_css/): Inlines the CSS a page uses, loads the rest async.
- [Prioritize critical images (prioritize_critical_images)](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/filters/prioritize_critical_images/): Sets fetchpriority=high on the LCP image.
- [Recompress JPEG (recompress_jpeg)](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/filters/recompress_jpeg/): JPEG-specific recompression.
- [Recompress PNG (recompress_png)](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/filters/recompress_png/): PNG-specific recompression.
- [Recompress WebP (recompress_webp)](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/filters/recompress_webp/): WebP-specific recompression.
- [Remove comments (remove_comments)](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/filters/remove_comments/): Strips HTML comments.
- [Resize images (resize_images)](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/filters/resize_images/): Resizes images to match <img> dimensions.
- [Responsive images (responsive_images)](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/filters/responsive_images/): Generates srcset for multiple resolutions.
- [Minify CSS (rewrite_css)](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/filters/rewrite_css/): Minifies CSS, rewrites embedded URLs.
- [Minify external JavaScript (rewrite_javascript_external)](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/filters/rewrite_javascript_external/): Minifies external JavaScript files.
- [Minify inline JavaScript (rewrite_javascript_inline)](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/filters/rewrite_javascript_inline/): Minifies inline JavaScript.
- [Sprite images (sprite_images)](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/filters/sprite_images/): Combines CSS background images into sprites.
- [Trim URLs (trim_urls)](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/filters/trim_urls/): Shortens URLs relative to base URL.
- [Extend cache (extend_cache)](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/filters/extend_cache/): Content-hashed URLs with a 1-year browser cache for CSS, images and scripts.
- [Recompress images (recompress_images)](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/filters/recompress_images/): Recompresses and converts images in every format (enables the sub-filters).
- [Optimize images (rewrite_images)](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/filters/rewrite_images/): Master image optimization: recompress, convert, resize and inline (enables the sub-filters).
- [Minify JavaScript (rewrite_javascript)](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/filters/rewrite_javascript/): Minifies external and inline JavaScript (enables both sub-filters).

## Operate

- [Run in production](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/deployment/): Run mod_pagespeed in production: Docker Compose, Kubernetes with or without the chart, the packaged systemd unit, permissions, logs and cache sizing.
- [ASP.NET Core in production](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/production-deployment/): Production deployment of the mod_pagespeed ASP.NET Core middleware: configuration, health probes, multi-instance scale and zero-downtime restarts.
- [mod_pagespeed admin console](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/admin-console/): mod_pagespeed admin console: alerts, statistics, cache inspection, message history and config, with setup and access control for nginx, Apache and IIS.
- [Use the web console](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/workbench/): Inspect cache contents, monitor live throughput and bandwidth savings, and hot-reload configuration from the mod_pagespeed web console at /console/.
- [Browser analysis with headless Chrome](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/browser-analysis/): How the optimizer worker renders pages in headless Chrome to extract critical CSS, find the LCP element, measure JS coverage and gate visual regressions.
- [Monitoring](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/monitoring/): Monitor mod_pagespeed: the admin console, the worker health socket and /v1/health, /v1/stats and Prometheus /v1/metrics, logs, and what to alert on.
- [Uninstall and rollback](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/uninstall/): Remove mod_pagespeed per shape (apt, dnf, cPanel, Docker, Helm, IIS, NuGet), what each leaves behind, cache cleanup, and rolling back a release.
- [Security hardening guide](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/security/): Security guidance for mod_pagespeed: restricting admin pages, domain authorization, untrusted content, CSS/XSS, cache poisoning, HTTPS, CVE patching.
- [Troubleshoot common issues](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/troubleshooting/): Fix common mod_pagespeed issues: cache misses, images not converting to WebP or AVIF, the optimizer worker not processing, and socket diagnostics.

## Agents

- [Serve Markdown to AI agents](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/agent-optimize/): Serve AI agents a rendered Markdown copy of your pages at the same URL, and synthesize an /llms.txt — off by default, nothing leaves your server.
- [Verify AI crawlers with Web Bot Auth](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/web-bot-auth/): Check RFC 9421 signatures from AI crawlers at your origin and label each request with a verified bot identity — observe-only, off by default.
- [Validate RSL license capability tokens](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/rsl-cap/): Validate Authorization: License capability tokens at your origin and return 401/402/pass — experimental operator access control, off by default.

## Reference

- [API reference: IPC, sockets, and C API](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/api-reference/): mod_pagespeed internal interfaces: the module-to-worker IPC wire format, the health and management sockets, the capability mask and the ps_ C API.
- [Call the worker HTTP API](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/http-api/): Optimizer worker HTTP API for mod_pagespeed: health, stats, Prometheus metrics, cache management, live config and WebSocket streaming, all via curl.
- [Release notes](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/release-notes/): mod_pagespeed release notes: the current release, the notes of every line, every release in one list, security updates and what changed since upstream.
- [License](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/license/): mod_pagespeed is licensed under the Apache License 2.0. We sell support; Priority and Enterprise add a private package repository (being set up).
- [PageSpeed filters reference](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/filters/): The image, CSS, JavaScript, HTML, and caching filters, what each one does, and which run by default.

## Release notes by line

- [Release notes: 2.6](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/release-notes-2-6/): mod_pagespeed 2.6.0 release notes: security fixes for the nginx and Apache modules, and an optimizer service that can start after the web server.
- [Release notes: 2.5](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/release-notes-2-5/): mod_pagespeed 2.5 release notes: 2.5.2, a security update for the bundled nginx and libpng, and 2.5.0, with one version number from then on.
- [Release notes: 2.4](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/release-notes-2-4/): mod_pagespeed 2.4.0 release notes: the module and the optimizer worker as one release (packages 1.19.0), with several rule packs and a security fix.
- [Release notes: 2.3](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/release-notes-2-3/): mod_pagespeed 2.3.0 release notes: the module and the optimizer worker as one release (packages 1.18.0), with rule packs and security fixes.
- [Release notes: 2.2](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/release-notes-2-2/): mod_pagespeed 2.2.0 release notes: the module and the optimizer worker as one release (packages 1.17.0), its security fixes and what changed.
- [Release notes: 2.1](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/release-notes-2-1/): mod_pagespeed 2.1.0 release notes: the first release of the module and the optimizer worker as one product (packages 1.16.0), with hardened defaults.
- [Release notes: the 2.0 optimizer worker](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/release-notes-2-0/): Release notes for the 2.0 optimizer worker line, 2.0.0-beta.1 to 2.0.42: each out-of-process optimizer release before the lines converged in 2.1.0.
- [Release notes: the 1.15 module](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/release-notes-1-15/): Release notes for the 1.15 module line, 1.15.0 to 1.15.0+r22: each Apache, nginx and IIS package revision before the lines converged in 2.1.0.
- [Release notes: the 1.1 module](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/release-notes-1-1/): Release notes for the 1.1 module line, 1.1.0-beta.1 to 1.1.0+r24: the first releases of the maintained module, before the renumber to 1.15.0 on 2026-06-01.

## Machine-readable

- [Product summary (JSON)](https://modpagespeed.com/api/product.json): Product, license, support tiers, image-format support per line and the related packages, as data.
- [llms-full.txt](https://modpagespeed.com/llms-full.txt): This index followed by the full Markdown text of every documentation page.
- [AI plugin manifest](https://modpagespeed.com/.well-known/ai-plugin.json): The model-facing description of the product.
- [Install recipes for coding agents](https://modpagespeed.com/recipes/README.md): One machine-first install recipe per server (nginx, Apache, cPanel, IIS, ASP.NET Core, Docker, Helm): prerequisites check, install, minimal configuration, a response-header verification and a rollback. The index defines the verification marker.
- [Recipe: nginx module](https://modpagespeed.com/recipes/nginx.md): The native nginx module from the signed package repository on the distribution's stock nginx; checks X-Page-Speed.
- [Recipe: Apache module](https://modpagespeed.com/recipes/apache.md): The native Apache module from the signed package repository, optimizer worker included; checks X-Mod-Pagespeed.
- [Recipe: cPanel / EasyApache 4](https://modpagespeed.com/recipes/cpanel.md): The signed ea-apache24-mod_pagespeed RPM on cPanel / WHM EasyApache 4 Apache, enabled in WHM; checks X-Mod-Pagespeed.
- [Recipe: IIS module](https://modpagespeed.com/recipes/iis.md): The signed MSI on Windows Server, checksum-verified, and a per-site pagespeed.config; checks X-Page-Speed.
- [Recipe: ASP.NET Core middleware](https://modpagespeed.com/recipes/aspnet-core.md): The WeAmp.PageSpeed.AspNetCore NuGet package, Program.cs and appsettings.json; checks X-PageSpeed.
- [Recipe: Docker](https://modpagespeed.com/recipes/docker.md): The nginx reverse proxy and the optimizer worker in containers in front of an origin; checks X-PageSpeed.
- [Recipe: Helm](https://modpagespeed.com/recipes/helm.md): The pagespeed Helm chart in front of an origin Service; checks X-PageSpeed.
- [Recipe: diagnose an installed module or worker](https://modpagespeed.com/recipes/diagnose.md): Read-only checks of an installed module or optimizer worker: the response header, the health socket, API reads, admin pages and logs.

## Distribution

- Signed apt and yum repository at https://packages.modpagespeed.com/ (GPG key https://packages.modpagespeed.com/pubkey.gpg; one-time setup `curl -fsSL https://packages.modpagespeed.com/install.sh | sudo sh`): `mod-pagespeed` (the Apache module), `nginx-module-pagespeed` (the nginx module, prebuilt and pinned to each distribution's stock nginx: Debian 12 bookworm (nginx 1.22.1), Debian 13 trixie (nginx 1.26.3), Ubuntu 22.04 jammy (nginx 1.18.0), Ubuntu 24.04 noble (nginx 1.24.0), amd64 + arm64; AlmaLinux 9 via yum against stock nginx 1.20.1) and `pagespeed-optimizer` (the optimizer worker). Current release: mod_pagespeed 2.6.0 (2026-10-28). See [the apt/yum repository](https://modpagespeed.com/download/apt-yum/) and [Install the module on Apache and nginx](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/installation-module/).
- Container images on GHCR: `ghcr.io/we-amp/pagespeed-nginx:2.6.0` (nginx with the module) and `ghcr.io/we-amp/pagespeed-worker:2.6.0` (the optimizer worker), on ubuntu:24.04. See [Install with Docker](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/installation-docker/).
- Helm chart `pagespeed` from the repository `https://modpagespeed.com/charts` (`helm repo add weamp https://modpagespeed.com/charts`; index at https://modpagespeed.com/charts/index.yaml; application version 2.6.0; Kubernetes 1.28+, 1.29+, 1.30+; Helm 3.12+). See [Deploy with Helm](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/helm-deployment/).
- IIS: the signed Windows installer, 2.6.0, on the module's GitHub release: https://github.com/We-Amp/mod_pagespeed/releases/download/module-v2.6.0/pagespeed-iis-2.6.0-win-x64.msi (Windows Server 2016 or later; IIS 10; x64). See [Install on IIS](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/install-iis/).
- NuGet `WeAmp.PageSpeed.AspNetCore` 2.6.0, the ASP.NET Core middleware (net8.0, net10.0; linux-x64, linux-arm64, osx-arm64, win-x64): `dotnet add package WeAmp.PageSpeed.AspNetCore`. See [Install ASP.NET Core middleware](https://modpagespeed.com/docs/aspnet-getting-started/).
- NuGet `WeAmp.PageSpeed.Sidecar` with `WeAmp.PageSpeed.Sidecar.NativeAssets.Linux`, 1.17.0, the module as an ASP.NET Core sidecar (linux-x64, linux-arm64; bundles nginx 1.30.4): `dotnet add package WeAmp.PageSpeed.Sidecar`.
- Worker packages (deb, rpm and Windows zip, with a checksum list) of every release: the [release listing](https://github.com/We-Amp/pagespeed-optimizer/releases/latest). The module packages install from the signed repositories above; see [Download](https://modpagespeed.com/download/).
